questions.prompt: The general praised his own soldiers, who had fought bravely.
questions.answer: Dux mīlitēs suōs laudāvit, quī fortiter pugnāverant.

questions.prompt: My son, why do you fear the anger of your father?
questions.answer: Mī fīlī, cūr īram patris tuī timēs?

questions.prompt: Our leaders defended the city with their own weapons.
questions.answer: Ducēs nostrī urbem armīs suīs dēfendērunt.

questions.prompt: The queen loved her husband, but his brother hated her.
questions.answer: Rēgīna coniugem suum amābat, sed frāter eius eam ōderat.

questions.prompt: Their houses were destroyed by fire, but ours remained unharmed.
questions.answer: Domūs eōrum igne dēlētae sunt, sed nostrae incolumēs mānsērunt.

questions.prompt: The mother embraced her daughter, whom she had not seen for many years.
questions.answer: Māter fīliam suam complexa est, quam multōs annōs nōn vīderat.

questions.prompt: Your words, o citizens, moved my heart deeply.
questions.answer: Verba vestra, ō cīvēs, animum meum vehementer mōvērunt.

questions.prompt: The king rewarded his own friends but punished their enemies.
questions.answer: Rēx amīcōs suōs remūnerātus est, sed inimīcōs eōrum pūnīvit.

questions.prompt: My dear son, follow your own judgment, not the opinion of the crowd.
questions.answer: Mī fīlī cāre, iūdicium tuum sequere, nōn opīniōnem vulgī.

questions.prompt: The birds defend their own nests against the serpent.
questions.answer: Avēs nīdōs suōs contrā serpentem dēfendunt.

questions.prompt: We love our fatherland more than our own lives.
questions.answer: Patriam nostram magis quam vītam nostram amāmus.

questions.prompt: The poet recited his verses, and the listeners praised them.
questions.answer: Poēta versūs suōs recitāvit, et audītōrēs eōs laudāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The consul, relying on his own strength, refused their help.
questions.answer: Cōnsul, suīs vīribus frētus, auxilium eōrum recūsāvit.

questions.prompt: Return my sword to me, for it is a gift of my father.
questions.answer: Gladium meum mihi redde, nam est patris meī dōnum.

questions.prompt: The girls carried their baskets full of flowers to the temple.
questions.answer: Puellae calathōs suōs flōribus plēnōs ad templum tulērunt.

questions.prompt: Caesar praised his legions and increased their pay.
questions.answer: Caesar legiōnēs suās laudāvit et stīpendium eārum auxit.

questions.prompt: The merchant hid his gold, fearing the greed of the soldiers.
questions.answer: Mercātor aurum suum abdidit, mīlitum avāritiam timēns.

questions.prompt: Our ancestors handed down these laws to us.
questions.answer: Maiōrēs nostrī hās lēgēs nōbīs trādidērunt.

questions.prompt: The woman praised the virtue of her husband, but despised his brother.
questions.answer: Fēmina virtūtem coniugis suī laudāvit, sed frātrem eius contempsit.

questions.prompt: The drunken debtor, cheating his creditors, squandered his own wealth.
questions.answer: Dēbitor ēbrius, crēditōrēs suōs fraudāns, opēs suās dissipāvit.

questions.prompt: Follow your own counsel, my son, and despise the words of the malicious.
questions.answer: Tuum cōnsilium sequere, mī fīlī, et verba malignōrum contemne.

questions.prompt: Our leader, relying on his own sword, led away the captured king.
questions.answer: Dux noster, ēnse suō frētus, rēgem captum abdūxit.

questions.prompt: Your vines, o farmers, were broken by the wind, but ours remained.
questions.answer: Vītēs vestrae, ō agricolae, ventō frāctae sunt, sed nostrae mānsērunt.

questions.prompt: The king loved his own daughter more than his whole kingdom.
questions.answer: Rēx fīliam suam plūs quam rēgnum suum tōtum amābat.

questions.prompt: The soldier, wounded in his own arm, could not raise his sword.
questions.answer: Mīles, in bracchiō suō vulnerātus, ēnsem suum tollere nōn potuit.

questions.prompt: You praised your teacher, but her books you never read.
questions.answer: Magistrum vestrum laudāvistis, sed librōs ejus numquam lēgistis.

questions.prompt: The general, trusting his own soldiers, scorned the threats of the enemy.
questions.answer: Dux mīlitibus suīs cōnfīsus hostium minās sprēvit.

questions.prompt: The king summoned the poet, but did not praise his verses.
questions.answer: Rēx poētam arcessīvit, sed versūs ejus nōn laudāvit.

questions.prompt: My son, guard our home while I am away.
questions.answer: Mī fīlī, domum nostram custōdī dum absum.

questions.prompt: The citizens praised their own laws but feared their neighbors' power.
questions.answer: Cīvēs lēgēs suās laudāvērunt sed vīcīnōrum potentiam timuērunt.

questions.prompt: Soldiers, remember your ancestors and defend your fatherland bravely.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs, majōrēs vestrōs mementōte et patriam fortiter dēfendite.

questions.prompt: The woman loved her husband, and his brother often helped her.
questions.answer: Mulier virum suum amābat, et frāter ejus eam saepe adjuvābat.

questions.prompt: Our commander led his own troops across the river by night.
questions.answer: Imperātor noster cōpiās suās trāns flūmen nocte trādūxit.

questions.prompt: Give me your hand, my friend, and trust my promises.
questions.answer: Dā mihi manum tuam, mī amīce, et prōmissīs meīs crēde.
